editorial:
Imagine moving to a big, busy city with your cousins to start your life over. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow Aju, Divya, and Kuttan as they land in Bangalore. Each of them is dealing with their own baggage, from family pressure to heartbreak. The vibe is super cozy and feels like a warm hug. It is not just about the city, but about how these three grow up and find themselves while navigating love and friendship. You will feel like you are part of their friend group from the very first scene.

The acting is what really makes the movie work because the chemistry between the leads feels totally real. The pacing is steady, though it feels more like a slice-of-life story than a high-energy thriller. One small downside is that some parts might feel a bit slow if you want constant action, but the emotional payoffs are worth it. If you want something feel-good, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best colors, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you love collecting physical discs.
endingExplained: In the end, the characters finally stop living for others. Divya chooses her own happiness over an arranged marriage and finds love with Das. Aju moves past his anger and finds a way to be successful on his own terms. Kuttan learns to be confident and finds a partner who truly appreciates him. They all grow into mature adults, realizing that family and self-love are the most important things in life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about friendship, family bonds, and finding yourself in a new city.
